title: From composition claim to source-grounded explanation
body:
# Start with the concrete question

The composer has found a likely implementation relationship while reading a Pull Request. When it asks for a Walkthrough, what keeps that candidate claim from silently becoming a published fact? Start at the [composer handoff boundary](rvw-ref:composer-handoff): one bounded brief carries both authoring authority over the question and implementation assertions that remain claims to verify.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  actor Caller
  participant Composer as rvw-review-compose
  participant WalkthroughProducer as rvw-walkthrough
  participant Source as committed source
  Caller->>Composer: request PR-wide composition
  Composer->>WalkthroughProducer: one brief with bounds and candidate claims
  WalkthroughProducer->>Source: inspect semantic evidence
  Source-->>WalkthroughProducer: committed text and tests
  WalkthroughProducer->>WalkthroughProducer: compare evidence with the bounded question
  alt source supports an answer inside the boundary
    WalkthroughProducer-->>Composer: grounded or corrected result
  else essential claim would change the question
    WalkthroughProducer-->>Composer: conflict, do not publish
    Composer->>Composer: revise brief or choose another surface
  end
```

The single Composer-to-producer handoff and its two kinds of input are grounded by the [composer contract](rvw-ref:composer-handoff). The producer's own comparison, corrected-answer branch, and no-publication branch come from the [Walkthrough producer's verification boundary](rvw-ref:walkthrough-verification); the repository supplies evidence but does not make the authoring decision. The relationship-map producer applies the same epistemic split but retains a different representation boundary in the [Structure producer contract](rvw-ref:structure-verification). The diagram shows one representative handoff, not every operation-specific preflight or an assurance that production always succeeds. `Source` is an explanatory participant for the committed repository, not a single source element, so it is deliberately not bound. Messages and branches are likewise evidenced by these nearby code references rather than by invented edge bindings.

# Update the mental model

After checking those ranges, the local model is small: the composer can decide *what question to ask* and *what is in scope*; it cannot decide that an implementation claim is true. The producer may return a source-supported correction inside the same boundary, or return an essential conflict without publication so the composer can recompose. [Static contract assertions](rvw-ref:contract-guard) lock that distinction into the repository, but their presence alone does not prove that a live producer invocation or publication was executed.

# Continue into the code

Next inspect the distribution boundary, because native activation only works if the expected siblings are actually packaged. The [canonical Skill list](rvw-ref:bundled-skill-set) includes the composer and both producers, and [package-root discovery](rvw-ref:package-root-discovery) requires every listed `SKILL.md` before installation can proceed. Read the remaining installer methods only if the next question is about local divergence, forced replacement, or atomic copying; those mechanics are outside this Walkthrough's authority-and-verification question.

references.description: Treats the brief's scope as authority and implementation assertions as claims that may be corrected or rejected.

references.description: Applies the same evidence boundary while owning one relationship-space representation.

references.description: Checks that the bundled composer text distinguishes authoring authority from semantic proof.

references.description: Accepts a package root only when every listed Skill entrypoint exists and resolves an install source from it.
